sinks.description: Google BigQuery — one table per stream, atomic overwrite or keyed MERGE upsert
sinks.name: bigquery

params.description: Dataset every stream's table lands in
params.name: bq_dataset

params.description: GCP project id that owns the dataset
params.name: bq_project

params.description: Service-account key JSON, inline. Pass it with --param-env from a secret store; copy this template and switch `auth` to application_default to use ADC instead.
params.name: bq_sa_key

sinks.description: Local JSON Lines files, one per stream — the local validation destination
sinks.name: jsonl

params.description: Directory to write <source>/<stream>.jsonl under
params.name: out_dir

sinks.description: PostgreSQL — one auto-mapped table per stream, transactional overwrite or ON CONFLICT upsert
sinks.name: postgres

params.description: Schema every stream's table is created in
params.name: pg_schema

params.description: postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db connection URL
params.name: pg_url

sinks.description: Local SQLite database — one auto-mapped table per stream, real overwrite/upsert semantics without infrastructure
sinks.name: sqlite

params.description: Database file (created if missing)
params.name: sqlite_path

sources.description: Example — two CSV exports as two streams (runs offline, no credentials)
sources.name: example-csv

params.description: Directory holding orders.csv and customers.csv
params.name: data_dir

sources.description: Example — a bearer-authenticated REST API with cursor pagination and one stream per endpoint
sources.name: example-rest-api

params.description: Bearer token
params.name: api_token

params.description: API root, e.g. https://api.example.com/v1
params.name: base_url

sources.description: GitHub — a repository's issues, issue comments, pull requests, commits, releases, Actions workflow runs, contributors and metadata
sources.name: github

params.description: API root — https://<host>/api/v3 for GitHub Enterprise Server
params.name: api_base_url

params.description: Repository owner — a user or organization login
params.name: github_owner

params.description: Repository name
params.name: github_repo

params.description: Fine-grained personal access token (or GitHub App installation token) with read access to the repository
params.name: github_token

sources.description: Google Ads — campaigns, ad groups, ads, and daily campaign / ad group / keyword performance over a rolling window (Google Ads API v22, GAQL)
sources.name: google-ads

params.description: API root — override only to replay recorded fixtures
params.name: api_base_url

params.description: Account to read, 10 digits without dashes
params.name: google_ads_customer_id

params.description: Google Ads API developer token (API Center of a manager account)
params.name: google_ads_developer_token

params.description: Manager account the credentials act through, 10 digits without dashes — the customer id itself for direct access
params.name: google_ads_login_customer_id

params.description: OAuth client id (Google Cloud console)
params.name: google_client_id

params.description: OAuth client secret
params.name: google_client_secret

params.description: OAuth refresh token with the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords scope
params.name: google_refresh_token

params.description: OAuth token endpoint — override only to replay recorded fixtures
params.name: google_token_url

params.description: Rolling window the performance streams re-read each run (conversions settle for days)
params.name: performance_window

sources.description: HubSpot CRM — contacts, companies, deals, tickets, products, owners and deal pipelines (CRM v3), properties lifted to columns
sources.name: hubspot

params.description: API root — override only to replay recorded fixtures
params.name: api_base_url

params.description: Comma-separated company properties to read
params.name: company_properties

params.description: Comma-separated contact properties to read
params.name: contact_properties

params.description: Comma-separated deal properties to read
params.name: deal_properties

params.description: Private app access token (Settings → Integrations → Private Apps)
params.name: hubspot_token

params.description: Comma-separated product properties to read
params.name: product_properties

params.description: Comma-separated ticket properties to read
params.name: ticket_properties

sources.description: Jira Cloud — issues (JQL enhanced search), projects, users, fields, statuses and issue types (REST API v3)
sources.name: jira

params.description: Comma-separated issue fields to return (`*navigable`, `*all`, or a list)
params.name: issue_fields

params.description: JQL selecting the issues to sync (must be bounded — the enhanced search rejects an unrestricted query)
params.name: issues_jql

params.description: Atlassian API token (id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens)
params.name: jira_api_token

params.description: Atlassian account email the API token belongs to
params.name: jira_email

params.description: Your Jira Cloud site, e.g. https://acme.atlassian.net
params.name: jira_url

sources.description: Meta Ads — ad account, campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives and daily ad-level insights via async report runs (Marketing API v24.0)
sources.name: meta-ads

params.description: API root — override only to replay recorded fixtures
params.name: api_base_url

params.description: Rolling date preset the insights stream re-reads each run (attribution settles for up to 28 days)
params.name: insights_window

params.description: System-user (or long-lived user) access token with ads_read
params.name: meta_access_token

params.description: Ad account id, digits only (without the act_ prefix)
params.name: meta_ad_account_id

sources.description: Salesforce — accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities, users, campaigns and tasks via Bulk API 2.0 (v62.0), incremental on SystemModstamp, soft deletes included
sources.name: salesforce

params.description: Connected app consumer key
params.name: salesforce_client_id

params.description: Connected app consumer secret
params.name: salesforce_client_secret

params.description: Your org's My Domain URL, e.g. https://acme.my.salesforce.com
params.name: salesforce_instance_url

params.description: OAuth host — https://test.salesforce.com for a sandbox
params.name: salesforce_login_url

params.description: OAuth refresh token for the integration user (scopes: api, refresh_token)
params.name: salesforce_refresh_token

sources.description: Shopify — orders, customers, products (incremental on updated_at), custom and smart collections and locations (Admin REST API 2025-07)
sources.name: shopify

params.description: Custom app Admin API access token (shpat_…)
params.name: shopify_access_token

params.description: Store admin root, e.g. https://acme.myshopify.com
params.name: shopify_store_url

params.description: Earliest update to read on the first run (RFC 3339)
params.name: start_date

sources.description: Stripe — customers, subscriptions, invoices, charges, refunds, payment intents, products, prices, payouts, balance transactions and events
sources.name: stripe

params.description: API root — override only to replay recorded fixtures
params.name: api_base_url

params.description: Secret or restricted API key (read-only restricted key recommended)
params.name: stripe_api_key

sources.description: Zendesk Support — tickets, users, organizations (incremental exports), groups, ticket metrics, satisfaction ratings and ticket fields
sources.name: zendesk

params.description: Earliest update to export on the first run (RFC 3339)
params.name: start_date

params.description: Zendesk API token (Admin Center → Apps and integrations → Zendesk API)
params.name: zendesk_api_token

params.description: Email of the agent/admin the API token belongs to
params.name: zendesk_email

params.description: Your Zendesk root, e.g. https://acme.zendesk.com
params.name: zendesk_url
